items.stem: You are assigning work to three coding agents. What most reduces the risk of conflicting changes?

options.text: Decompose the work into scoped tasks that touch mostly disjoint files
options.rationale: Correct: disjoint, well-scoped tasks minimise overlapping edits and conflicts.

options.text: Give all three the same broad task and merge whoever finishes first
options.rationale: Duplicated broad tasks create conflicting edits and wasted work.

options.text: Let each agent edit any file it wants
Skip branches and have them all commit to main
options.rationale: Committing to main removes isolation and protection.

items.explanation: Correct: disjoint, well-scoped tasks minimise overlapping edits and conflicts.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO controls keep multi-agent branches safe to integrate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Branch protection requiring passing checks before any agent branch merges
options.rationale: Correct: required checks gate every branch before it enters the shared line.

options.text: Human review of agent pull requests before merge
options.rationale: Correct: human review catches issues automated checks miss.

options.text: Allowing agents to adjust their own required checks
Merging all branches simultaneously without review
options.rationale: Simultaneous unreviewed merges invite conflicts and defects.

items.explanation: Correct: required checks gate every branch before it enters the shared line.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Each agent's branch passes its own tests. Why run integration tests before combining them?

options.text: Independently passing branches can still conflict or break shared behaviour once combined
options.rationale: Correct: integration tests catch interactions that per-branch tests cannot.

options.text: Integration tests are only for single-developer projects
options.rationale: They are especially important when multiple agents change the system.
Combined changes frequently interact in unexpected ways.

options.text: Integration testing replaces the need for human review
options.rationale: Tests and review are complementary, not substitutes.

items.explanation: Correct: integration tests catch interactions that per-branch tests cannot.
